summary: Configured sudo on node1 (Alpine Linux) to log every sudo command with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log via a sudoers.d drop-in (Defaults logfile=..., log_year, log_host, !syslog), keeping entries out of the general syslog/messages log. Verified logging works and confirmed no leakage into /var/log/messages, then performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id, rebooted via sudo, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and confirmed the sudoers config, prior log content, and continued correct logging behavior all survived the restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: Alpine Linux 3.23, sudo 1.9.17p2, syslogd running, no prior sudo-specific logging config in /etc/sudoers
Created /etc/sudoers.d/00-command-log with: Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log"; Defaults log_year, log_host, !syslog
Validated syntax with visudo -c, created log file with 0600 root:root permissions
Triggered test sudo commands and confirmed they appear in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with timestamp/user/command, and do not appear in /var/log/messages
Issued non-blocking reboot via sudo -n, received acknowledgement before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again; confirmed new boot_id (7631fc37-23dc-408f-a1b4-9436b96856f1), proving an actual restart occurred

Post-restart: verified sudoers drop-in persisted, visudo parses OK, prior log entries preserved (26 lines), new sudo commands post-reboot correctly logged to sudo-commands.log and absent from /var/log/messages

evidence.requirement: Sudo commands logged with user and timestamp to a dedicated file
evidence.summary: After installing the sudoers.d drop-in, /var/log/sudo-commands.log shows entries like 'Sep 29 08:05:10 2026 : root : HOST=node1 ; ... USER=root ; COMMAND=...' for visudo, touch, chmod, chown, whoami, cat commands.

evidence.requirement: Entries kept out of the general system log
evidence.summary: Step 7 output shows /var/log/messages contains only sudo entries from before the drop-in took effect (up through the 'install' command); none of the subsequent sudo commands (visudo, touch, chmod, chown, whoami, cat) leaked into messages.

evidence.requirement: Configuration persists and remains correct (sudoers validity, baseline)
evidence.summary: Baseline capture: no pre-existing syslog directive for sudo, visudo parsed OK, and pre-restart state of sudoers.d/00-command-log and log file recorded.
Captured boot_id 44767f03-0ec7-4fa9-a365-65d452b6d548, confirmed sudo-commands.log exists (16 lines) and sudoers drop-in present prior to reboot.
Backgrounded 'reboot' command via sudo -n returned 'ack returned' before the node disconnected.

evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Connection timed out on three consecutive polls (node down), then boot_id returned as 7631fc37-23dc-408f-a1b4-9436b96856f1 — different from the pre-restart boot_id, proving an actual reboot occurred.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of sudo logging configuration and data
evidence.summary: After restart: sudoers.d/00-command-log content intact, visudo -c parses OK, prior log entries preserved (26 lines), a new 'sudo id' command was correctly appended to sudo-commands.log, and it did not appear in /var/log/messages.
